drafted_from: tool:generate-images's row in tool-rows.json, do-work/generate_images.py, do-work/placeholder_image_provider.py, read-data/image_records.py and test/generate-images.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a picture of a red door with generate-images, using the placeholder provider first to check the chain, and keep it in a new folder called images." It writes the request file, runs the script on your computer and tells you where the picture is.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one request file and writes the images it gets back into a folder.
instructions: 1. Decide which program makes your images (a hosted model's caller or a local model's program) and which environment variables it reads for its key; put the names, never the key, in provider.env_names. To check the chain first, use the placeholder provider that ships with the tool.

2. Write a request file: {"request_id": "req 1", "prompt": "a red door", "requested_at": "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z", "provider": {"argv": ["python3", "trillion-workshop/tools/generate-images/do-work/placeholder_image_provider.py", "--request-json", "{request}", "--output-json", "{output}"]}}.

3. Say "Make an image with generate-images". Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:generate-images"} and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/generate-images/do-work/generate_images.py --request request.json --out images.

4. Read the last line it prints: {"result": ...} with kind image-generation.result names each image by path (a file in the folder) or url; kind image-generation.error gives a code and message (exit 2) and nothing is made up. Then swap the placeholder argv for your real provider's.

worked_examples.title: One placeholder picture for "a red door"
worked_examples.ask: Make a picture of a red door and keep it in the images folder.
worked_examples.given: From tools/generate-images/test/generate-images.test.mjs (the placeholder case), checked by running it here: the command python3 trillion-workshop/tools/generate-images/do-work/generate_images.py --request request.json --out images, where request.json holds request_id "req 1", prompt "a red door", requested_at "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z" and the placeholder provider argv from the instructions.
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line printed is {"result": {"kind": "image-generation.result", "request_id": "req 1", "prompt": "a red door", "provider_ref": "placeholder-image-provider", "format": "image/png", "output_artifact_refs": [{"media_type": "image/png", "byte_length": 569, "path": "req_1-1.png"}], "src": "req_1-1.png", "completed_at": "<the time the provider finished>"}} and exit status 0. The file images/req_1-1.png is a 569-byte solid-colour PNG; the same prompt always gives the same picture. With no provider in the request it prints image-generation.error code image_provider_missing instead and exits 2.
